questions.prompt: The THREE structural ingredients of a Singleton are:
options: Private constructor · static instance field · public static accessor (GetInstance)
questions.explain: **Private constructor** (nobody else news it) + **static _instance** + **static GetInstance()** with the lazy `if (_instance == null)` guard (locked for thread safety).

questions.prompt: Factory Method vs Abstract Factory — the key difference:
options: Factory Method creates ONE product by subtype choice; Abstract Factory creates FAMILIES of related products that stay consistent
Abstract Factory is just a renamed Factory Method
Abstract Factory can only make two products
questions.explain: FM: one creator method → one product hierarchy. **AF: a factory INTERFACE producing a coordinated SET** (button+menu+dialog per theme) — swap the whole family, never mix members.

questions.prompt: A report object needs title, optional header, optional footer, optional charts, optional appendix — building it has 20 constructor permutations. Pattern?
questions.explain: Telescoping-constructor pain + many OPTIONAL parts = **Builder**: fluent `.WithHeader(...).WithCharts(...).Build()`.

questions.prompt: A game spawns 10,000 enemies per level; constructing one from config files takes 50ms, but copying a configured template takes 0.1ms. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Prototype**: expensive creation → clone preconfigured templates. (The drill's version: user preference/theme objects, game-scaled.)

questions.prompt: The common purpose of ALL creational patterns is to:
options: Decouple clients from concrete classes and the mechanics of object creation
questions.explain: Creational patterns move `new` out of client code: clients depend on **abstractions**, creation logic is centralized/configurable — enabling OCP/DIP at the creation site.

questions.prompt: `public static PaymentGateway Create(string region) { return region == "MY" ? new MyGateway() : new GlobalGateway(); }` — this is:
options: A Factory Method choosing the concrete by runtime input
questions.explain: Creator method + runtime-input dispatch + clients receiving the BASE type = **Factory**. The client never mentions MyGateway/GlobalGateway.

questions.prompt: Why must the Singleton's constructor be PRIVATE?
options: To make GetInstance the ONLY creation path — a public constructor would allow multiple instances
questions.explain: The whole guarantee rests on the constructor being unreachable from outside; **GetInstance is the single gate**. (A favourite fill-in-the-line exam item — drill Q10's line 1.)

questions.prompt: In the theme example (DarkButton+DarkMenu vs LightButton+LightMenu), what specifically does Abstract Factory PREVENT?
options: Mixing members of different families (a DarkButton with a LightMenu)
questions.explain: Each concrete factory produces members of ONE family — clients can never accidentally combine across families, and swapping factories swaps the whole family consistently.
